fatal_errors: The proposed FCC/B2 lamellar intervention is not established as achievable in equiatomic FeNiCrMn; the cited evidence concerns an Al- and Co-containing AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy whose B2 phase is compositionally enabled by Ni-Al ordering.
Evidence from tensile tests on a different alloy at room and elevated temperatures is extrapolated to dynamic loading without any supporting strain-rate evidence.
The strain-rate range is unspecified, so the central claim of performance across strain rates is neither bounded nor testable.
The response replaces the target single-crystal FCC model with an unspecified as-cast multiphase alloy and therefore does not reconstruct the studied intervention or deformation regime.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad strength-ductility objective and proposes a recognizable composite-strengthening mechanism, but it does not match the hidden study. The target examines crystallographic loading direction, temperature from 10 to 600 K, and strain rates of 10^8–10^10 s^-1 in single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn. Its key findings concern anisotropic yield strength, thermal softening, rate-insensitive yielding, increased dislocation density at higher rates, and Shockley-partial-mediated stacking faults without BCC transformation or twinning. None of these are reconstructed. The proposed B2 lamellae, dislocation pinning mechanism, and 700 °C boundary come from a chemically distinct AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy and lack validation in Co-free FeNiCrMn. The falsification experiment is only generic tensile testing; it does not define dynamic strain rates, processing parameters, matched controls, or diffraction/TEM criteria confirming that B2 lamellae were actually produced. Thus it cannot separate failure of phase formation from failure of the claimed strengthening mechanism.
